text:
jamie: Thinking we should run a focused perf-quality sweep across FP8/INT4 variants before the next Dedicated rollout. We need canonicalization of configs so results are comparable across endpoints.

ravi: +1. What do you mean by canonicalization here?

jamie: Make a single source-of-truth for: model binary, quant profile, KV cache settings, attention slice size, and batching strategy. Then run the same input corpus and traffic shape. Otherwise noise kills signal.

sasha: Agreed. Also we should capture both intrinsic metrics (perplexity, BLEU-ish proxies) and extrinsic (chat satisfaction p95, hallucination-rate).

maria: Can we reuse the shadow-sampling harness? I can wire endpoint routing to shadow 10% of live traffic for a day.

jamie: Yes, shadow for a day + offline sweep with synthetic latency curves. Proposed CLI for batch runs:

```
# run canonical sweep
redwood-sweep run --models "m-1.fp32,m-1.fp8,m-1.int4" \
  --profiles "canonical.yaml" \
  --corpus ./sweeps/customer-sample-v2.jsonl \
  --traffic "burst=200,steady=50" \
  --out results/1792468000
```

alex: canonical.yaml should lock seed, sampling temp, topk/top_p, and system prompt variant. Also add a header indicating whether KV caching was warm.

ravi: How will we gate? What's the acceptance threshold for FP8/INT4 vs baseline?

jamie: Proposal: metric buckets: latency (p95), cost/tokens, quality signal (deg_score combining lm-qa, tokenwise-snr, and manual anchors). Gate if any of these:
- deg_score increase > 2.0 (unitless)
- hallucination-rate increase > 0.8% absolute
- latency p95 increase > 30ms or > 10% (whichever larger)

If any gate trips, auto-fallback to INT8-compat variant for the rollout.

sasha: The deg_score composition needs to be explicit. Otherwise different endpoints will interpret differently. We used: 0.6*lm-qa + 0.3*anchor-fail + 0.1*token-snr last time.

maria: For shadow routing: we should also capture user-agent slices (mobile vs web) and prompt-length buckets. Some degradations only show up at longctx.

ajamie: Good catch — add longctx (tokens>2048) bucket to sweep.

alex: Ops question: will this sweep create pressure on Dedicated GPU pools? We should throttle concurrency to avoid impacting production.

maria: I'll run shadow at 10% with concurrency cap 30 QPS per pool. Offline sweep can be in bench cluster.

ravi: Runtime integration: we need a canonical feedback signal the runtime can consume to flip precision. Something like: runtime-metrics -> quality-orch -> precision-decision. Is there an existing endpoint?

jamie: There's an existing quality-orch webhook but it's coarse. This sweep should produce a small JSON artifact per profile with these fields: profile, sample_count, deg_score_delta, hallucination_delta, latency_p95_delta, regression_examples[]. We'll store them in S3 and ops can point the orch to the artifact URL.

sasha: regression_examples[] must be small (<=10) and include: input, baseline_output, candidate_output, short diff, and a categorical tag (hallucination, omission, toxicity, formatting).

alex: For rollout strategy: canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 2h hold at each stage and health checks on deg_score + latency. Auto-roll-back if any metric crosses gate.

maria: We should also test staged quant-profile updates: the runtime needs to allow hot-swapping quant files or fall back to a compatible model variant. Is hot-swap reliable for INT4? We've seen OOM spikes before.

jamie: Note: INT4 needs extra workspace for per-token scaling in some kernels; make sure bench cluster uses same allocator. Add memory-profiling to sweep. If memory margin < 200MB average across runs, mark profile as "risky".

ravi: Ops-bot: can you create a temporary ticket to track sweep infra + owners?

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-6421: "perf-quality sweep infra + canonical profiles". Assignees: maria (shadow), jamie (sweep runner), sasha (quality metrics), alex (ops gating). ETA: 5 working days. :white_check_mark:

jamie: Action items:
- maria: wire shadow splits + concurrency caps (ETA 2d)
- jamie: generate canonical.yaml and run offline sweep (ETA 3d)
- sasha: formalize deg_score weights and the regression_examples schema (ETA 2d)
- alex: draft canary rollout and rollback automation (ETA 4d)

maria: I'll also add per-customer tagging. For big customers we might opt out of aggressive FP8 unless they sign up.

ravi: One more thing: we need to document what "compatible variant" means for the runtime. E.g., fp8->int8 mapping table and model signature checks. Otherwise the orch might pick an incompatible pair.

jamie: I'll add a small runtime-checker that compares model headers: {arch, dim, kv-format, quant-version} and fails fast if mismatch.

alex: If all good, let's schedule a short 30m sync after the first offline sweep to decide the first canary.

jamie: SG. I'll post results and link the S3 artifacts here when done.

maria: thanks all.

ops-bot: Deploy job queued: bench-cluster/sweeps/1792468000 (offline). Estimated runtime ~6h.
